name: IHL Group on ihlservices.com: Retail AI Forecasts, Readiness Index and Advisory Services
title: IHL Group on ihlservices.com: Retail AI Forecasts, Readiness Index and Advisory Services
answer: IHL Group's site publishes paid forecasts and advisory products on AI's economic impact in retail, including a Retail AI Forecast Model projecting a 23% compound annual growth rate for retail AI investment through 2029 and a $9.2 trillion worldwide value-creation estimate, plus a Retail AI Readiness Index ranking North American publicly traded retailers and ClearSight AI engagements that prioritise between 75 and 400 use cases.

sections.body: IHL Group publishes this material on ihlservices.com as a mix of commercial research products and advisory services. The pages read cover the Retail AI Forecast Model, the Retail AI Readiness Index 2026, AI Readiness Profiles for Retailers, three ClearSight AI advisory engagements, and two research reports, Retail's AI Revolution and Retail AI Scaling Readiness 2026. The forecast model spans 2022 to 2029 and is built on IHL's WorldView IT Sizing Forecast model. The readiness index covers North American publicly traded retailers, and the profiles cover nearly 200 North American public retailers and restaurant chains. Most items are sold, with the Retail's AI Revolution report offered as a free download.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The Retail AI Forecast Model projects the economic impact of Traditional AI/ML, Generative AI and Artificial General Intelligence on retail and hospitality from 2022 to 2029, broken out by AI type, segment, tier and more than 120 technology types, with charts on sales, gross margins and SG&A by region and tier. IHL projects a 23% compound annual growth rate for retail AI investment through 2029. The free Retail's AI Revolution report puts the cumulative worldwide economic impact of AI at $9.2 trillion through 2029, described as a demand-side value-creation estimate rather than a measure of AI software spending, with inventory intelligence, customer-facing AI and supply chain AI named as leading value categories. The Retail AI Readiness Index ranks North American publicly traded retailers by AI readiness and projected financial impact, excluding communications companies and fuel and convenience stores. AI Readiness Profiles go deeper for nearly 200 retailers, projecting annual sales, gross margin and SG&A impact by line of business and by specific solution. ClearSight AI engagements prioritise between 75 and 400 use cases across ten lines of business, rating legal and compliance, data and system readiness, output readiness, strategic importance and business value, and completing in 10 to 20 days.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: IHL projects a 23% compound annual growth rate for retail AI investment through 2029 and a $9.2 trillion cumulative worldwide economic impact from AI through 2029. The forecast model tracks more than 120 AI technology categories across 5 global regions and 11 retail segments, with tiers defined as Tier 1 over $1b in sales, Tier 2 $250m to $1b and Tier 3 under $250m. The model costs $2,500 for segments or $4,995 for enterprise access, and profiles cost $199 each or $2,500 annually. IHL cites RAND that 80% of AI projects fail, Gartner that less than 30% move past pilot, and Upwork that 75% of employees deploying generative AI saw productivity decrease. Its scaling research finds only 14% of retailers current on edge computing and 9% running active computer vision, though 40% have cameras mounted.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in retail, this source supplies quantified forecasts and benchmarks rather than vendor claims. The forecast model and the free report give a sizing of AI's financial impact across sales, gross margins and SG&A, split by AI type, region, tier and line of business, which is useful for framing investment cases. The readiness index and profiles let a reader compare named retailers on AI readiness and projected benefit. The ClearSight material documents a structured method for choosing among hundreds of use cases, including the failure rates that motivate it, and the scaling research identifies store infrastructure gaps that constrain deployment.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: The material is largely commercial. Most products carry prices and are sold as forecasts, indexes or advisory engagements, so the underlying data is only partly visible in the free pages. The readiness index and profiles cover North American publicly traded retailers and restaurant chains, with European expansion only planned, and the index excludes communications companies and fuel and convenience stores. The $9.2 trillion figure is explicitly a demand-side value-creation estimate, not a measure of AI software spending. Several pages are product descriptions rather than full research, and the cited failure statistics come from RAND, Gartner and Upwork rather than IHL's own fieldwork.
